sentences.en: You can't be having these terrible, these awful looking parties.
sentences.zh: 你不能举办这些看起来很糟糕的派对。

sentences.en: I mean, actually, to dignify them with the word parties is, if I went to a party,
sentences.zh: 我是说，实际上，用“派对”这个词来美化它们，如果我去参加一个派对，

sentences.en: if someone invited me to a party and it was Rishi Sunak standing there with a paper cup of Prosecco.
sentences.zh: 如果有人邀请我去参加一个派对，而里希·苏纳克站在那里拿着一个纸杯装的普罗塞克酒。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I'd be absolutely gutted.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我会感到非常沮丧。

sentences.en: But I think more than that, I think that COVID has – I think Britain, I think the entire global economy is suffering from long COVID.
sentences.zh: 但我认为不仅如此，我认为新冠疫情已经——我认为英国，我认为整个全球经济都在遭受长新冠的折磨。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然是这样。

sentences.en: Of course it is.
sentences.zh: 当然是这样。

sentences.en: I think, you know, to deal with that requires talents and qualities that Johnson massively does not possess.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道，处理这些问题需要约翰逊完全不具备的才能和素质。

sentences.en: Well, Tom, I think there's a couple of points to make there.
sentences.zh: 好吧，汤姆，我认为有几点需要说明。

sentences.en: So one of them is events, dear boy events, as Harold Macmillan famously said in the 1950s, are the challenge for any political leader.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是“突发事件，亲爱的，突发事件”，正如哈罗德·麦克米伦在20世纪50年代所说的那样，这是任何政治领导人面临的挑战。

sentences.en: So you sort of hear this with people, with politicians.
sentences.zh: 所以你经常从人们，从政治家那里听到这个。

sentences.en: They'll often say in their defence, well, I've been very unfortunate because, you know, events have ganged up on me.
sentences.zh: 他们经常会辩解说，好吧，我非常不幸，因为，你知道，突发事件联合起来对付我。

sentences.en: But, I mean, that's the nature of the job.
sentences.zh: 但是，我是说，这就是这份工作的本质。

sentences.en: When you move into the – It is.
sentences.zh: 当你搬进——确实如此。

sentences.en: When you go behind that desk, you know things are going to happen.
sentences.zh: 当你坐在那张桌子后面时，你知道事情会发生。

sentences.en: There will be wars, there will be crises, there will be economic shocks.
sentences.zh: 会有战争，会有危机，会有经济冲击。

sentences.en: That is the absolute – and if you're very lucky, if you're very, very lucky – actually, Tony Blair is a very good example, I think, of somebody who was generally very lucky.
sentences.zh: 这是绝对的——如果你非常幸运，如果你非常、非常幸运——实际上，托尼·布莱尔是一个很好的例子，我认为，他是一个通常非常幸运的人。

sentences.en: He had an economic – a run of kind of calm waters, no storms – the storMs.
sentences.zh: 他经历了一段经济——一段平静的水域，没有风暴——风暴。

sentences.en: The Antonine Peace.
sentences.zh: 安东尼时代的和平。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: There were storMs.
sentences.zh: 确实有风暴。

sentences.en: I mean, 9-11.
sentences.zh: 我是说，9·11事件。

sentences.en: I mean, his own decision to invade Iraq.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他自己入侵伊拉克的决定。

sentences.en: But, economically, he had fantastically plain sailing.
sentences.zh: 但是，在经济上，他一帆风顺。

sentences.en: Any prime minister in the early 2020s would have had difficulties, but that is the nature of the job.
sentences.zh: 2020年代初的任何首相都会遇到困难，但这就是工作的本质。

sentences.en: I mean, Franklin Roosevelt in America in the 30s, Thatcher in the 80s.
sentences.zh: 我是说，30年代美国的富兰克林·罗斯福，80年代的撒切尔。

sentences.en: You know, events happen.
sentences.zh: 你知道，突发事件会发生。

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: But, you know, if you compare, say, Asquith or Chamberlain or Churchill, who obviously faced the worst crises of all.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，如果你比较一下，比如说阿斯奎斯、张伯伦或丘吉尔，他们显然面临着最严重的危机。

sentences.en: I actually think that Johnson is quite well suited to dealing with, you know, wars.
sentences.zh: 我实际上认为约翰逊非常适合处理，你知道，战争。

sentences.en: I think he's had quite a good invasion of Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 我认为他在乌克兰入侵事件中表现得相当不错。

sentences.en: Yeah, but that's because he doesn't have to organise anything, is that Tom?
sentences.zh: 是的，但那是因为他不需要组织任何事情，是这样吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: But he can make the right decision.
sentences.zh: 但他可以做出正确的决定。

sentences.en: And also, to give him credit, you know, he has been – he was kind of ahead of the curve with that.
sentences.zh: 而且，为了给他记功，你知道，他一直——他在那方面有点超前。

sentences.en: He was alert to it.
sentences.zh: 他对此保持警惕。

sentences.en: So, that is something, I think, that he got right.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这是他做对的一件事。

sentences.en: I just think that a massive public health crisis – I suspect he has no interest in hospitals or doctors or, you know, vaccines.
sentences.zh: 我只是认为一场大规模的公共卫生危机——我怀疑他对医院、医生或，你知道，疫苗没有兴趣。

sentences.en: It's just – I think it completely leaves him cold.
sentences.zh: 这只是——我认为这让他完全感到冷漠。

sentences.en: I think he's just not interested.
sentences.zh: 我认为他只是不感兴趣。

sentences.en: I think there's another element to this, which is that a really successful, high-end politician – I mean, that thing about Reagan, politicians are actors.
sentences.zh: 我认为这还有另一个因素，那就是一个真正成功的、高端的政治家——我是说，关于里根的那件事，政治家就是演员。

sentences.en: They are public performers.
sentences.zh: 他们是公众表演者。

sentences.en: I mean, that must have been true in the Roman world.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这在罗马世界一定也是真的。

sentences.en: I mean, it obviously was true in the Roman world, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这在罗马世界显然是真的，不是吗？

sentences.en: One of the most famous bits of Roman political theatre, Mark Antony giving Caesar's funeral oration, is pure performance, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 罗马政治戏剧中最著名的片段之一，马克·安东尼发表凯撒的葬礼演说，纯粹是表演，不是吗？

sentences.en: But I think a good politician is capable of playing more than one part.
sentences.zh: 但我认为一个好的政治家有能力扮演不止一个角色。

sentences.en: So, Boris was clearly very good at playing a particular part, which is the kind of roguish mountebank.
sentences.zh: 所以，鲍里斯显然非常擅长扮演一个特定的角色，那就是那种流氓骗子。

sentences.en: And British politics has been littered with those.
sentences.zh: 英国政坛充斥着这样的人。

sentences.en: So, we talked about that, didn't we, in our episode on how Prime Ministers fall?
sentences.zh: 所以，我们谈过这个，不是吗，在我们关于首相如何下台的那一集中？

sentences.en: And you drew analogies with Disraeli, with –
sentences.zh: 你把迪斯雷利与——

sentences.en: Yeah, Disraeli, Lloyd George, Blair to some extent.
sentences.zh: 是的，迪斯雷利、劳合·乔治、布莱尔在某种程度上。

sentences.en: Palmerston.
sentences.zh: 帕默斯顿。

sentences.en: Harold McMillan was the kind of actor manager.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德·麦克米伦是那种演员经理。

sentences.en: I mean, Palmerston.
sentences.zh: 我是说，帕默斯顿。

sentences.en: In that Unheard piece that you mentioned, I quoted Karl Marx about Palmerston.
sentences.zh: 在你提到的那篇《Unheard》文章中，我引用了卡尔·马克思关于帕默斯顿的话。

sentences.en: So, Karl Marx said of Palmerston, if not a good statesman of all work, he's at least a good – Not a very good accent, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 所以，卡尔·马克思谈到帕默斯顿说，如果不是一个全能的好政治家，他至少是一个好的——口音不太好，多米尼克。

sentences.en: I'm not doing your terrible Karl Marx accent.
sentences.zh: 我没有在模仿你那糟糕的卡尔·马克思口音。

sentences.en: Because, I mean –
sentences.zh: 因为，我是说——

sentences.en: Go on.
sentences.zh: 继续。

sentences.en: I mean, people will just have to imagine that in your hair flick.
sentences.zh: 我是说，人们只需要在你的甩发动作中想象一下。

sentences.en: In your hair flick.
sentences.zh: 在你的甩发动作中。

sentences.en: Well, you're cluso.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你是克鲁索。

sentences.en: I thought that was very cluso, you're Karl Marx.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那非常克鲁索，你是卡尔·马克思。

sentences.en: So, Karl Marx said, in my voice, if not a good statesman of all work, he's at least a good actor of all work.
sentences.zh: 所以，卡尔·马克思用我的声音说，如果不是一个全能的好政治家，他至少是一个全能的好演员。

sentences.en: He succeeds in the comic as in the heroic.
sentences.zh: 他在喜剧和英雄角色中都取得了成功。

sentences.en: He's not a first-class orator, but an accomplished debater.
sentences.zh: 他不是一流的演说家，但却是一位出色的辩论家。

sentences.en: And it goes on,
sentences.zh: 而且还在继续，

sentences.en: Being an exceedingly happy joker, he ingratiates himself with everybody.
sentences.zh: 作为一个极其快乐的小丑，他赢得了所有人的好感。

sentences.en: Never losing his temper, he imposes on an impassioned antagoniSt.
sentences.zh: 从不发脾气，他能压制激情的对手。

sentences.en: When unable to master a subject, he knows how to play with it.
sentences.zh: 当无法精通某一学科时，他懂得如何玩转它。

sentences.en: If wanting in general views, he's always ready to weave a web of elegant generalities.
sentences.zh: 如果缺乏宏观视野，他总是准备好编织一张优雅的概论之网。

sentences.en: And this sort of persona for Palmerston worked very well, because there's a lovely story about him going with the Speaker of the House of Commons to the Great Exhibition in 1851.
sentences.zh: 帕默斯顿的这种人设非常奏效，因为有一个关于他与下议院议长一同参加1851年万国工业博览会的精彩故事。

sentences.en: And the Speaker says, As we walked along, I could gauge the popularity of Lord Palmerston.
sentences.zh: 议长说，当我们走过时，我能感受到帕默斯顿勋爵的受欢迎程度。

sentences.en: The moment he came in sight throughout the whole building, men and women, young and old, at once were struck as if by an electric shock.
sentences.zh: 当他出现在整个建筑内的一瞬间，无论男女老少，都仿佛受到了电击一般。

sentences.en: Lord Palmerston!
sentences.zh: 帕默斯顿勋爵！

sentences.en: Here's Lord Palmerston!
sentences.zh: 帕默斯顿勋爵在那儿！

sentences.en: Bravo!
sentences.zh: 好啊！

sentences.en: Hurrah!
sentences.zh: 万岁！

sentences.en: Lord Palmerston forever!
sentences.zh: 帕默斯顿勋爵万岁！

sentences.en: So it went on throughout the whole building.
sentences.zh: 整个建筑里一直都在欢呼。

sentences.en: But that's like Johnson at the Olympics.
sentences.zh: 但这就像奥运会上的约翰逊。

sentences.en: That is Johnson at the Olympics.
sentences.zh: 那确实就是奥运会上的约翰逊。

sentences.en: That's precisely the point.
sentences.zh: 这正是重点所在。

sentences.en: He was an entertainer.
sentences.zh: 他是个艺人。

sentences.en: He was a showman, as Palmerston was, as Disraeli was, as Lloyd George was.
sentences.zh: 他是个表演家，就像帕默斯顿、迪斯雷利和劳合·乔治一样。

sentences.en: But all of those three men all had other parts that they played.
sentences.zh: 但他们三个人也都扮演过其他角色。

sentences.en: So Palmerston, you know, he's not just the sort of the showman at home.
sentences.zh: 所以帕默斯顿，你知道，他不仅仅是在国内那种表演家。

sentences.en: He's also the imperialist abroad.
sentences.zh: 他在国外也是个帝国主义者。

sentences.en: Disraeli is also a reformer.
sentences.zh: 迪斯雷利也是一位改革家。

sentences.en: He's also the romantic noveliSt.
sentences.zh: 他也是一位浪漫主义小说家。

sentences.en: He's also all these other things.
sentences.zh: 他还有很多其他身份。

sentences.en: Lloyd George, he's an absolute philanderer and disgraceful man.
sentences.zh: 劳合·乔治，他是个彻头彻尾的浪子，是个卑劣的人。

sentences.en: But he's also a passionate reformer.
sentences.zh: 但他也是一位充满激情的改革家。

sentences.en: He's also a brilliant committee chairman.
sentences.zh: 他也是一位出色的委员会主席。

sentences.en: He combines the Michael Gove and the Boris Johnson, if you like.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，他结合了迈克尔·戈夫和鲍里斯·约翰逊的特点。

sentences.en: He can do all the nuts and bolts.
sentences.zh: 他能处理所有琐碎的实务。

sentences.en: And that's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, Tony Blair could play different parts.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，托尼·布莱尔也能扮演不同的角色。

sentences.en: Margaret Thatcher could.
sentences.zh: 玛格丽特·撒切尔也能。

sentences.en: In America, I mean, Reagan could play different parts, obviously, and he had done all his life.
sentences.zh: 在美国，我的意思是，里根显然也能扮演不同的角色，他一生都在这样做。

sentences.en: Roosevelt could.
sentences.zh: 罗斯福也能。

sentences.en: I think Boris, if he was an actor with a casting agency, there's only one part he can play.
sentences.zh: 我认为鲍里斯，如果他是一个演员，在一家选角公司，他只能演一个角色。

sentences.en: He can't do anything else.
sentences.zh: 他演不了别的。

sentences.en: And I think that's where he was found out.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是他被看穿的地方。

sentences.en: Well, and that was the whole problem with COVID.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这也是新冠疫情带来的全部问题。

sentences.en: Because he couldn't stand there.
sentences.zh: 因为他无法站在那里。

sentences.en: And, you know, he'd say, you know, my thoughts are with everyone who's, you know, suffering and everything.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他会说，我的心与每一个正在受苦的人同在，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But he just couldn't make it sound plausible.
sentences.zh: 但他就是无法让这些话听起来可信。

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Even though he himself had very, you know, almost died of it.
sentences.zh: 尽管他自己也曾，你知道，差点因此丧命。

sentences.en: Even after that, he couldn't really.
sentences.zh: 即使在那之后，他依然无法真正做到。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's interesting how even after that, because that's sort of completely forgotten now, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，即使在那之后，因为那件事现在似乎完全被遗忘了，不是吗？

sentences.en: That he was, wasn't he, he went to hospital.
sentences.zh: 他当时确实，不是吗，他进了医院。

sentences.en: He nearly died, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想他差点就死了。

sentences.en: And he was, you know, he was in trouble with it.
sentences.zh: 而且他当时，你知道，他因为那件事陷入了困境。

sentences.en: But that's disappeared from our national memory, because it doesn't, and he doesn't really play on that himself, because he hates playing the victim.
sentences.zh: 但这已经从我们的国民记忆中消失了，因为他自己并不怎么拿这件事做文章，因为他讨厌扮演受害者。

sentences.en: A different, with a different political persona.
sentences.zh: 一个不同的，带有不同政治人设的（人）。

sentences.en: That might loom larger in that sort of sense of them.
sentences.zh: 那在某种意义上可能会显得更重要。

sentences.en: Joey, our producer, is sending us a message to say, is he the last prime minister that the general public would most want to have a pint with?
sentences.zh: 我们的制作人乔伊发来消息问，他是普通大众最想一起喝杯啤酒的最后一位首相吗？

sentences.en: I mean, that having the pint thing, they have the same thing in America, but they use the same formula when they're talking about politicians.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那种“一起喝杯啤酒”的事情，在美国也有，但他们在谈论政客时也用同样的公式。

sentences.en: And I think it really matters.
sentences.zh: 我认为这真的很重要。

sentences.en: I mean, nobody wanted to have a drink with Theresa May, did they?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，没人想和特蕾莎·梅喝一杯，对吧？

sentences.en: Probably not really with Keir Starmer either.
sentences.zh: 可能基尔·斯塔默也不太行。

sentences.en: Would you go for a drink with Jeremy Corbyn?
sentences.zh: 你会和杰里米·科尔宾去喝一杯吗？

sentences.en: No, probably not.
sentences.zh: 不，大概不会。

sentences.en: But you would go for a drink.
sentences.zh: 但你会去喝一杯的。

sentences.en: I mean, actually, I was talking to somebody the other week, who knows Boris Johnson, and has known him for a long time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，实际上，上周我和一个认识鲍里斯·约翰逊很久的人聊天。

sentences.en: And he said to me, he was telling me all, everything that was wrong with him.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我关于他的一切缺点。

sentences.en: And, you know, he went through the whole list of all the failings and all these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他列举了他所有的失败和各种各样的事情。

sentences.en: And then he said, he said, the weird thing about him is he is obviously a terrible man in all these different ways.
sentences.zh: 然后他说，关于他最奇怪的一点是，他在所有这些方面显然都是个糟糕的人。

sentences.en: But if he came in now and he pulled up a chair at this table, he would be such good company.
sentences.zh: 但如果他现在走进来，在这张桌子旁拉把椅子坐下，他会是一个非常好的伙伴。

sentences.en: And we would have such a tremendous time.
sentences.zh: 我们会度过一段非常棒的时光。

sentences.en: And he would be so fun to be with.
sentences.zh: 和他在一起会非常有趣。

sentences.en: And that's the sort of the paradox of him.
sentences.zh: 这就是他身上的那种矛盾之处。

sentences.en: Well, that's what people responded to.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是人们所回应的东西。

sentences.en: People clearly sense that.
sentences.zh: 人们显然感觉到了这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's why he's one mayor, you know, the mayor and all that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想这就是他成为市长的原因，你知道，市长之类的。

sentences.en: So two questions for you before we go.
sentences.zh: 在我们结束之前，有两个问题要问你。

sentences.en: The first is, has he inflicted serious damage on the idea of the mos maiorum?
sentences.zh: 第一个是，他是否对“祖宗之法”（mos maiorum）的理念造成了严重损害？

sentences.en: The idea of the unwritten British constitution being governed by convention,
sentences.zh: 即不成文的英国宪法受惯例约束的理念，

sentences.en: by a kind of understanding that politicians of all shapes and sizes will be governed by an accepted morality, an accepted sense of what chaps should do, that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 通过一种共识，即各种背景的政客都将受到公认的道德、公认的“君子所为”准则的约束，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Has he has he inflicted serious damage on that?
sentences.zh: 他是否对此造成了严重损害？

sentences.en: That's an excellent question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极好的问题。

sentences.en: Or has the fact that Britain's unwritten constitution has in the long run withstood him, kind of, you know, evacuated him, as it were, voided him,
sentences.zh: 还是说，英国不成文宪法从长远来看经受住了他的考验，可以说，把他“排泄”掉了，清除了他，

sentences.en: showing that it's still functioning.
sentences.zh: 这反而证明了它依然在发挥作用。

sentences.en: And the second question is, will he be seen as a historically significant prime minister?
sentences.zh: 第二个问题是，他会被视为一位具有历史意义的首相吗？

sentences.en: Oh, that's two brilliant questions, Tom.
sentences.zh: 哦，那是两个精彩的问题，汤姆。

sentences.en: You should ask questions more often.
sentences.zh: 你应该多问问问题。

sentences.en: So the first one, I would probably say, some listeners may disagree with this, but I think the conventions are intact.
sentences.zh: 关于第一个问题，我可能会说，有些听众可能不同意，但我认为惯例是完好的。

sentences.en: I think he has obviously tested them and he's broken a lot of them.
sentences.zh: 我认为他显然考验了它们，也打破了其中许多。

sentences.en: But as you say, the fact that he has been evacuated by the system, it's very telling, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，他被系统“排泄”掉的事实，非常能说明问题，不是吗？

sentences.en: That in the end, virtually every single senior conservative either came out against him or just stayed silent and refused to support him.
sentences.zh: 最终，几乎每一位资深保守党人要么公开反对他，要么保持沉默并拒绝支持他。

sentences.en: And the ones who did support him were the ones who would only ever have got a job.
sentences.zh: 而那些支持他的人，都是些只会为了保住饭碗的人。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, he was left at this point.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他当时已经众叛亲离了。

sentences.en: I mean, if Nadine Doris and Jacob Rees-Mulker listeners to this podcast, I'd be quite surprised.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果娜丁·多里斯和雅各布·里斯-莫格在听这个播客，我会感到非常惊讶。

sentences.en: But also, you know, I think it's nice to be inclusive to our listeners.
sentences.zh: 但同时，你知道，我认为对听众保持包容是件好事。

sentences.en: So I apologize to them for what I'm about to say.
sentences.zh: 所以我为我接下来要说的话向他们道歉。

sentences.en: But I mean, if the two, these two utter clowns are the only people you have left supporting you and everybody else on every wing of the party.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，如果这两个彻头彻尾的小丑是你仅剩的支持者，而党内各个派系的其他所有人……

sentences.en: So from Steve Baker on the kind of libertarian right to Jeremy Hunt on the kind of remainer left of the Tory party.
sentences.zh: 从自由意志主义右翼的史蒂夫·贝克，到保守党内留欧派左翼的杰里米·亨特。

sentences.en: People of such diverse views are coming out against you and saying, you've broken the conventions, you have to go.
sentences.zh: 观点如此迥异的人们都站出来反对你，说你打破了惯例，你必须离开。

sentences.en: Then clearly something is wrong.
sentences.zh: 那么显然是有什么地方出了问题。

sentences.en: And I think actually it's hard to, the fact that he's been punished, as it were, so publicly, humiliated, actually, Tom.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为实际上很难……他被如此公开地惩罚、羞辱的事实，实际上，汤姆。

sentences.en: He's been humiliated for breaking the conventions, for lying, for sending out ministers to say things that would, and he's clearly infuriated them.
sentences.zh: 他因为打破惯例、撒谎、派遣部长去说那些话而受到羞辱，他显然激怒了他们。

sentences.en: And somebody, I was having my hair cut today in the bar, and I were chatting about, you know, he sort of said, well, politicians, they're all the same, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 今天我在理发店理发时，有人跟我聊天，他大概说，嗯，政客们，他们都一样，不是吗？

sentences.en: They're all liars and all this sort of thing, which is, of course, what people always say.
sentences.zh: 他们都是骗子，诸如此类，这当然是人们常说的话。

sentences.en: But actually, in some ways, what's happened in the last few days shows whatever you think of politicians, what they think of themselves.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，在某些方面，过去几天发生的事情表明，无论你如何看待政客，他们是如何看待自己的。

sentences.en: I mean, a lot of them have talked, those Tories like Javid, have talked about their integrity.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们中的许多人，像贾维德那样的保守党人，谈论过他们的诚信。

sentences.en: Now, you may well think, or the listeners may think, oh, they've got no integrity anyway.
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能认为，或者听众可能认为，哦，他们本来就没什么诚信。

sentences.en: But they clearly think they do, and that, you know, the Prime Minister has traduced that or has tarnished it.
sentences.zh: 但他们显然认为自己有，而且，你知道，首相损害或玷污了这一点。

sentences.en: So I think, actually, the conventions, they still, a lot, most of them, the vast majority, still clearly believe in those conventions.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，实际上，惯例，它们依然……大多数人，绝大多数人，显然仍然相信这些惯例。

sentences.en: So I don't think it's analogous to what happened on the 6th of January 2021 in America.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这与2021年1月6日发生在美国的事情不可同日而语。

sentences.en: No, well, that's absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 不，嗯，那绝对不是。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, people are sort of, have always made this comparison between Donald Trump and Boris Johnson that I actually never, ever thought was right,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，人们总是把唐纳德·特朗普和鲍里斯·约翰逊做这种比较，我实际上从来没觉得是对的，

sentences.en: because I thought they're such totally different political personalities.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得他们是完全不同的政治人物。

sentences.en: I mean, they've both got blonde hair, and they're both populists.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们都有金发，而且都是民粹主义者。

sentences.en: And as you said about the abortion debate, Britain is not America.
sentences.zh: 正如你关于堕胎辩论所说的那样，英国不是美国。

sentences.en: Not everything has to be seen through an American prism.
sentences.zh: 并非所有事情都必须通过美国的棱镜来看待。

sentences.en: And this is not really like...
sentences.zh: 而且这并不是真的像……

sentences.en: No, this has been about the testing of the limits of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 不，这关乎对宪法极限的考验。

sentences.en: I would also make up what I'm sure many listeners will regard as a kind of insane perspective.
sentences.zh: 我还要提出一个我相信许多听众会认为是疯狂的观点。

sentences.en: But I actually think that every country at the moment is massively hurting.
sentences.zh: 但我实际上认为，目前每个国家都在遭受巨大的痛苦。

sentences.en: The after effects of COVID and the impact of energy price rises means that every country is going through a terrible, terrible stage.
sentences.zh: 新冠疫情的后遗症和能源价格上涨的影响，意味着每个国家都在经历一个非常、非常糟糕的阶段。

sentences.en: And I think that it's kind of right and proper that leaders who don't measure up to the gravity of the times, you know, go and someone else be brought in.
sentences.zh: 我认为，那些无法衡量时代严峻性的领导人，你知道，离开并换上其他人，是正确且恰当的。

sentences.en: And I think in that sense, actually, the British Constitution is kind of showing that it works.
sentences.zh: 我认为从这个意义上说，实际上，英国宪法正在证明它是有效的。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, it's working even in the most very basic sense.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，即使在最基本的意义上，它也在运作。

sentences.en: He's lost the confidence of the House of Commons.
sentences.zh: 他失去了下议院的信任。

sentences.en: He's got to go.
sentences.zh: 他必须走人。

sentences.en: It's as simple as that.
sentences.zh: 就这么简单。

sentences.en: But I agree with you.
sentences.zh: 但我同意你的看法。

sentences.en: A different prime minister.
sentences.zh: 一位不同的首相。

sentences.en: What would also be good, I think, there's been a lot of heat in British politics in the last seven years, six, seven years.
sentences.zh: 我认为还有一件好事，过去七年，六、七年里，英国政治中充满了火药味。

sentences.en: I think a slightly lower temperature would be good for Britain.
sentences.zh: 我认为稍微降低一点温度对英国有好处。

sentences.en: But again, I mean, in reaction to that, again, you know, Britain has been going through an unprecedentedly tumultuous time.
sentences.zh: 但同样，我的意思是，作为对那件事的反应，你知道，英国一直在经历一段前所未有的动荡时期。

sentences.en: And the perspective from abroad is, you know, what on earth is going wrong?
sentences.zh: 国外的视角是，你知道，到底出了什么问题？

sentences.en: Everything seems to be going wrong.
sentences.zh: 一切似乎都在出错。

sentences.en: But again, you could say that this reflects quite well on British democracy, because actually every country should be going through a terrible time.
sentences.zh: 但同样，你可以说这反映了英国民主相当不错的一面，因为实际上每个国家都应该在经历一段糟糕的时期。

sentences.en: Every country is facing incredible stresses and strains and challenges and kind of existential questions.
sentences.zh: 每个国家都面临着难以置信的压力、紧张、挑战和某种生存问题。

sentences.en: And in a sense, the fact that, you know, we've had so many elections, so many weird referendums, I mean, all kinds of mad shit happening left, right and centre.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，你知道，我们举行了这么多选举，这么多奇怪的公投，我的意思是，各种疯狂的事情在左右两边发生。

sentences.en: I mean, it should be, mad shit should be happening, because we're living through the age of mad shit.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，应该发生疯狂的事情，因为我们正生活在疯狂的时代。

sentences.en: Tom, this is top punditry.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这是顶级的评论。

sentences.en: But actually, I completely agree with you.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我完全同意你的看法。

sentences.en: I completely agree with you.
sentences.zh: 我完全同意你的看法。

sentences.en: I think a rambustious, colourful, chaotic democracy is better, as long as the sort of, you know, as long as the temperature doesn't rise too much.
sentences.zh: 我认为一个喧闹、多彩、混乱的民主制度更好，只要，你知道，只要温度不要升得太高。

sentences.en: As long as it doesn't go for the full 1640s.
sentences.zh: 只要它不重蹈1640年代的覆辙。

sentences.en: We don't want that.
sentences.zh: 我们不想要那个。

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: But a rambustious democracy in which crazy things happen is not a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 但一个疯狂事情频发的喧闹民主制度并不是坏事。

sentences.en: And I think the contrast that people classically make is they say,
sentences.zh: 我认为人们经典地做出的对比是他们说，

sentences.en: look at Britain with these sort of terrible clans and these ludicrous developments and look at Germany with such wonderful stability and all of these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 看看英国这些糟糕的派系和荒谬的发展，再看看德国那种美妙的稳定和所有这些东西。

sentences.en: And, of course, it's very tempting for us in Britain to look across the channel at Germany and say, oh, isn't this admirable and stuff.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们英国人隔着海峡看德国，说“哦，这难道不令人钦佩吗”之类的，是非常诱人的。

sentences.en: On the other hand, you look, I mean, Angela Merkel, who we did a whole podcast about Angela Merkel and German chancellors and her legacy.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，你看，我的意思是，安格拉·默克尔，我们做过一整期关于安格拉·默克尔、德国总理和她的遗产的播客。

sentences.en: I mean, that looks pretty dodgy now, that period of kind of complacent stagnation, if you like,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那段时期现在看起来相当可疑，那种自满停滞的时期，如果你愿意这么说的话，

sentences.en: ending with the Nord Stream deal with Russia and this sort of virtual appeasement of Vladimir Putin.
sentences.zh: 以与俄罗斯的北溪协议和对弗拉基米尔·普京的这种事实上的绥靖政策而告终。

sentences.en: Now, the new guy looks like he's a bank manager from a small town of Wiltshire.
sentences.zh: 现在，这个新人看起来像个威尔特郡小镇的银行经理。

sentences.en: No offence, Tom.
sentences.zh: 无意冒犯，汤姆。

sentences.en: Absolutely nothing wrong with that.
sentences.zh: 那绝对没什么错。

sentences.en: But, you know, who's, again, got what looks like a pretty dodgy record.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，他，同样，有着看起来相当可疑的记录。

sentences.en: You could argue, on Russia, you could argue that actually a bit of a rumbustious democracy that more countries could do with it.
sentences.zh: 关于俄罗斯，你其实可以说，那种稍微有点喧闹的民主，可能正是更多国家所需要的。

sentences.en: And in a way, the fact that it is farcical and chaotic and whatnot, I don't think that's necessarily a terrible thing.
sentences.zh: 而且在某种程度上，它那种荒诞、混乱等等的特质，我觉得未必是一件坏事。

sentences.en: That's what it is.
sentences.zh: 事实就是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, Johnson is a kind of Prince Regent figure.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，约翰逊就像是一个摄政王式的人物。

sentences.en: People in the 18th century, Tom, would look at what was happening now and they'd say, this is absolutely standard.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，18世纪的人如果看到现在发生的一切，他们会说，这完全是常规操作。

sentences.en: This is completely fine.
sentences.zh: 这完全没问题。

sentences.en: Now, that's Boris Johnson's place in history.
sentences.zh: 这就是鲍里斯·约翰逊在历史上的定位。

sentences.en: He's going to go down as quite a short-lived prime minister.
sentences.zh: 他会被记作一位任期相当短暂的首相。

sentences.en: So he's down there.
sentences.zh: 所以他就在那个行列里。

sentences.en: Same time as Chamberlain, I think, to the day.
sentences.zh: 我想他和张伯伦的任期差不多长，甚至精确到天。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's down there right now with Chamberlain.
sentences.zh: 没错，他现在就和张伯伦并列。

sentences.en: And I think it's quite possible, and wouldn't this be the most sort of delicious irony, that he may not match Theresa May's time in office, which would be very amusing.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得很有可能——这难道不是最绝妙的讽刺吗——他可能连特蕾莎·梅的任期都比不上，那可就太搞笑了。

sentences.en: So will he be remembered?
sentences.zh: 那么他会被人们记住吗？

sentences.en: I think he definitely will be remembered because he's a character.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他肯定会被记住，因为他是个很有个性的人。

sentences.en: And British – most prime ministers – we've talked about this so many times – most prime ministers are completely and utterly forgotten.
sentences.zh: 而英国——大多数首相——我们已经讨论过很多次了——大多数首相都被彻底遗忘了。

sentences.en: So who remembers the Earl of Derby?
sentences.zh: 那么谁还记得德比伯爵？

sentences.en: Who remembers Sir Alex Douglas Hume?
sentences.zh: 谁还记得亚历克·道格拉斯-休姆爵士？

sentences.en: Nobody.
sentences.zh: 没人记得。

sentences.en: Frankly, who under the age of 40 remembers Harold Wilson?
sentences.zh: 坦白说，40岁以下的人里有谁记得哈罗德·威尔逊？

sentences.en: Or James Callaghan.
sentences.zh: 或者詹姆斯·卡拉汉。

sentences.en: Or James – well, who does remember James – who remembers Stanley Baldwin, Tom?
sentences.zh: 或者詹姆斯——好吧，谁还记得詹姆斯——汤姆，谁还记得斯坦利·鲍德温？

sentences.en: It pains me to say it, but nobody does.
sentences.zh: 我很痛苦地承认，没人记得。

sentences.en: If you ask 20 people in the street who was Stanley Baldwin, they'd say that he played for Bolton Wanderers in the early 1950s.
sentences.zh: 如果你在街上问20个人斯坦利·鲍德温是谁，他们会说他是20世纪50年代初效力于博尔顿流浪者队的球员。

sentences.en: Oh, he does have that sound.
sentences.zh: 哦，他确实听起来像个球员。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, I think very few – Thatcher is remembered.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你知道，我觉得很少有人——撒切尔夫人会被记住。

sentences.en: Churchill is remembered.
sentences.zh: 丘吉尔会被记住。

sentences.en: Maybe Blair will be remembered.
sentences.zh: 也许布莱尔会被记住。

sentences.en: Cameron, no.
sentences.zh: 卡梅伦，不会。

sentences.en: May, no.
sentences.zh: 梅，不会。

sentences.en: Boris Johnson.
sentences.zh: 鲍里斯·约翰逊。

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: Boris Johnson will be remembered as a character.
sentences.zh: 鲍里斯·约翰逊会作为一个个性鲜明的人物被记住。

sentences.en: He'll be remembered for Brexit.
sentences.zh: 他会因为脱欧而被记住。

sentences.en: And he'll also possibly be remembered for the chaotic nature of his departure.
sentences.zh: 而且他可能还会因为他离任时那种混乱的场面而被记住。

sentences.en: But other than that – And he may be remembered for being the Prime Minister during COVID, if COVID is remembered.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外——如果新冠疫情能被记住的话，他可能还会因为在新冠疫情期间担任首相而被记住。

sentences.en: But will COVID be remembered?
sentences.zh: 但新冠疫情会被记住吗？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, how many people remembered the Spanish flu before COVID struck?
sentences.zh: 我是说，在新冠疫情爆发前，有多少人记得西班牙流感？

sentences.en: I think it depends what the long-term legacy of COVID is, which I think is too early to tell.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这取决于新冠疫情的长期影响是什么，但我认为现在下结论还为时过早。

sentences.en: But, I mean, will our grandchildren care about COVID?
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，我们的孙辈会在乎新冠疫情吗？

sentences.en: I mean, if the long-term legacy is that –
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果它的长期影响是——

sentences.en: Well, if they're looking back and studying, you know, what are the causes of the Third World War?
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果他们回头研究，你知道，第三次世界大战的起因是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: Well, I think the truth of the matter is, let's imagine our grandchildren doing British history in the early 21st century at school.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我认为事实是，让我们想象一下我们的孙辈在学校里学习21世纪初的英国历史。

sentences.en: And the sort of weariness with which they will plod through the essay questions on the Cameron years and austerity and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们会带着那种厌倦感，苦苦钻研关于卡梅伦时期和紧缩政策之类的论文题目。

sentences.en: Or Theresa May and the details of her various Brexit deals.
sentences.zh: 或者特蕾莎·梅以及她各种脱欧协议的细节。

sentences.en: And then they'll turn the page and there'll be a picture of Boris Johnson dangling.
sentences.zh: 然后他们翻过这一页，就会看到一张鲍里斯·约翰逊悬在半空的照片。

sentences.en: Unquestionably dangling from that zip wire with his Union Jack flags.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，就是他挂在滑索上，手里挥舞着英国国旗的那张。

sentences.en: And they will breathe a colossal sigh of relief, much as you would if you were about to study Charles James Fox.
sentences.zh: 他们会如释重负地长舒一口气，就像你准备学习查尔斯·詹姆斯·福克斯时那样。

sentences.en: And you say, great, finally a good character.
sentences.zh: 你会说，太好了，终于有个有趣的人物了。

sentences.en: This is going to be a laugh.
sentences.zh: 这下有乐子了。

sentences.en: And you do a week on Boris Johnson.
sentences.zh: 然后你花一周时间研究鲍里斯·约翰逊。

sentences.en: And it probably would be quite disobliging to him.
sentences.zh: 那可能对他来说不太恭敬。

sentences.en: But it would be fun.
sentences.zh: 但那会很有趣。

sentences.en: Now, he probably didn't want – I think deep down he didn't want to go down in history as a joker.
sentences.zh: 现在，他可能并不想——我觉得在内心深处，他不想作为一个小丑被载入史册。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He wanted to go down as a great man, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 他想作为一位伟人被铭记，不是吗？

sentences.en: But that's Fortuna's joke.
sentences.zh: 但这就是命运的玩笑。

sentences.en: It is Fortuna's joke.
sentences.zh: 确实是命运的玩笑。

sentences.en: So we should end with a prediction.
sentences.zh: 所以我们应该以一个预测来结束。

sentences.en: So who do you think – I'm going to put you on the spot – who do you think will be Prime Minister at the end of this calendar year?
sentences.zh: 那么你认为——我要让你当场预测一下——你认为今年年底谁会是首相？

sentences.en: Oh, I thought you were going to say at the end of this week.
sentences.zh: 哦，我还以为你要说这周末结束时呢。
